A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 23-page versions of the same MoH paper. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification, image-generation and language-model experiments, including ablations, efficiency measurements and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original MoH experiments and their outcomes, including Tables 1-7 and the empirical analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 4.4 retain the same head routing, shared heads, two-stage weighting, training losses and procedure for adapting LLaMA3.

E1.justification: The datasets and tasks are unchanged. Table 4's corrected headings identify benchmarks already documented in Section 4.4 and Appendix E; they do not establish added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline membership, including TransNeXt, DiT, vanilla LLMs, LLaMA3-8B and the stage-one model in Table G.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged. The corrected few-shot labels in Table 4 match settings already described in v2.

E4.justification: Component and head-ratio ablations, attention-similarity measurements, training-progress plots and routing analyses are retained unchanged, including the appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical result entries, plotted trends and generated examples are unchanged. Table 4 retains every score; its corrected headings clarify existing results rather than introduce new outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10), Appendix A.1's gradient-based specialization argument and Table B's attention-similarity definition are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same efficiency, performance and pretrained-model adaptation claims, including the headline 64.0% average accuracy using 75% of attention heads.

C2.justification: Interpretations of head specialization, task-dependent redundancy and Chinese/math forgetting are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the same limitations and future directions.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information is unchanged, including Appendix B's hyperparameters, data mixtures, vocabulary details and code links.

R1.justification: The references, Section 2's related-work discussion and Section 5's comparison with MoA are unchanged. No cited works or research-positioning claims are added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes from v2, 14 June 2025, to v3, 1 December 2025. The narrative, terminology, section order and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 corrects duplicated headings: its second block becomes HellaSwag, LogiQA, BoolQ, LAMBADA and SciQ; its third becomes PIQA, WinoGrande, NQ, ARC-C and Average. Limited table resizing and surrounding text reflow accompany this correction; all figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 incorrectly repeats the first benchmark-heading row across all three blocks of Table 4. v3 supplies the appropriate headings, including Average, making the main LLaMA3 comparison clearer and preventing misattribution of scores. This is a useful reporting correction; the scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
